newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-TAMPA LOOSES, LEAVING D.C. UNITED LONE UNBEATEN TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TAMPA LOOSES, LEAVING D.C. UNITED LONE UNBEATEN TEAM.

text.p: Defending champion D.C. United remained the only undefeated team in Major League Soccer after the New England Revolution stunned the Tampa Bay Mutiny 2-1 on Sunday.

Darren Sawatzky broke a 1-1 tie with 13 minutes remaining in front of a crowd of 57,407 in the Revolution home opener, which was the second game of a doubleheader at Foxboro Stadium. The U.S. and Mexico played to a 2-2 draw in a World Cup qualifier in the opener.

New England coach Thomas Rongen, who directed the Mutiny to a league-best 20-12 record last season, avenged a 4-0 loss to his former team on April 6. The Revolution (2-2) moved out of last place in the Eastern Conference past the New York/New Jersey MetroStars.

Argentine Alberto Naveda had given the Revolution a 1-0 lead, but Tampa Bay (3-1) equalised on a goal by Brazilian Joao Batista. Defender Alexi Lalas played in both games, starting for the U.S. National Team and coming on as a late substitute in the nightcap.
United (4-0) remained unbeaten behind a 2-1 victory over the MetroStars (1-4) in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

El Salvadoran international Raul Diaz Arce and Bolivian Jaime Moreno scored in the opening eight minutes. Venezuelan National Team forward Giovanni Savarese had the MetroStars' lone goal after a quick free kick by Colombian Antony DeAvila.
The Los Angeles Galaxy recorded its first victory after three consecutive losses with a 2-1 comeback win over the Colorado Rapids (1-4) in Pasadena, California.

Ecuadoran international Eduarto Hurtado, who finished with 21 goals last season and was held without a shot in his previous two games, scored his first of the season in the 60th minute and Brazilian Welton added the game-winner seven minutes later.
Mark Chung broke a 1-1 tie in the 80th minute to lift the Kansas City Wizards (3-1), the Western Conferenced leaders, to a 2-1 triumph over the Dallas Burn (2-3) in Kansas City, Missouri, on Friday.
Frank Klopas had given Kansas City the lead, redirecting a shot by former Scottish international Mo Johnston into the net in the 22nd minute. The Burn equalised on Gerell Elliott's goal.

The Burn bounced back with a 4-1 victory over Colorado on Sunday as Dante Washington scored a goal in each half in Dallas. Temoc Suarez and Elliott also tallied for Dallas. Henderson converted a penalty kick for the Rapids.

The Columbus Crew recorded a 2-1 shootout win over the San Jose Clash (2-3) in Columbus, Ohio. Reserve goalkeeper David Winner, playing in place of Brad Friedel, on U.S. National Team duty, made three saves in the shootout as Todd Yeagley converted the game-winner. Pete Marino scored for Columbus during regulation, Jeff Baicher for San Jose.
